title: Frontend: Rock Paper Scissor
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Rock Paper Scissor. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({opponent="rock"}). Rock, Paper, Scissors buttons[data-choice] resolve a round against the injected opponent. Output [data-testid=result] win/draw/loss and [data-testid=wins] counts wins. Reset clears both. Standard cyclic rules apply.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Generate the opponent choice in the user-action handler, then derive win/draw/loss from a small outcome table.
alternativeApproaches: Add best-of-N rounds with a terminal match state and an unambiguous restart action.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: All nine choice pairs; repeated rounds; draw.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
